messages.subject: inla.spde.make.A
parts:
Hi,

I want to do spatial prediction using a model with two likelihoods, but I am not sure if the matrix A is well defined. 
Can you help me please? Here is part of my code:


coords_mesh_obs<-rbind(mesh$loc[,1:2],coords_obs)
A<-inla.spde.make.A(mesh,coords_mesh_obs)

z1<-c(rep(NA,nv),z)
y1<-c(rep(NA,nv),y)

stk.z <- inla.stack(tag='z',
                    data=list(r=cbind(z1, NA)), 
                    A=list(A, 1),
                    effects=list(
                      list(i.z=1:spde$n.spde),
                      list(z.b0=rep(1,nv+n),
                           z.cov=cov)))

stk.y <- inla.stack(tag='y',
                    data=list(r=cbind(NA, y1)), 
                    A=list(A, 1),
                    effects=list(
                      list(i.y=1:spde$n.spde,
                           i.y2=1:spde$n.spde),
                      list(y.b0=rep(1,nv+n),
                           y.cov=cov)))

stk.zy <- inla.stack(stk.z, stk.y)


Here the dimension of A is (nv+n) x (nv). 

Any help is welcome.
Thank you.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.spde.make.A
parts:
Hi,
Need more information to tell if that’s wrong or right.

What’s the meaning of n and nv?
What’s the number of observations from each likelihood model?
What’s the intent of the pre-padding of y1 and z1 with NAs?
Are the covariate defined for each mesh node, or for each observation?

Finn

Thank you for your fast reply.

n - number of observations
nv - number of mesh nodes

The number of observations is n for each likelihood model.
I want to get predictions at mesh nodes locations, that’s why I added NAs in y1 and z1.
The covariate is defined for each mesh node and for each observation. Its length is nv+n.
